Problem Formulation

The Entity Resolution Challenge

Three independent data sources contain real-world businesses with severe typographic noise, legal suffix permutations, missing PIN codes, and spelling inconsistencies.

Source 1: Deduplicated References

Contains 2,206,821 training entities and 1,732,544 test entities. Each entity is guaranteed unique within Source 1. An entity may have 0 matches (singletons), exactly 1 match, or multiple matches across S2 and S3.

Source 2 & 3: Noisy Targets

Combined 10.3M training records and 9.9M test records. Suffers from legal suffix variations (Inc, LLC, Pvt Ltd, SA, GmbH), phonetic misspellings, and fragmented addresses.

Official Macro F0.5 Metric

Precision is weighted 2× over Recall (\(F_{0.5} = \frac{1.25 \cdot P \cdot R}{0.25 \cdot P + R}\)). False merges are severely penalized. Correctly predicting an empty list for singletons receives a full score of 1.0.

Official Orientation & System Specifications

The Complete Business Entity Resolution Guide

Full technical synthesis of all 6 video modules: mathematical scoring formulations, multi-pass blocking mechanics, dataset partitioning, two-deliverable protocols, and anti-cheating compliance.

Video Module 01 • Problem Anatomy

Real-World Catalog Fragmentation & Multi-Vendor Ingestion

Slide 1 & 2

When an enterprise signs up on Amazon Business, core profile attributes are captured (legal name and physical address). To enrich the catalog, records are ingested from independent external data vendors (Source 2 and Source 3). Because these external providers use disparate naming conventions, abbreviations, OCR engines, and localized landmarks, they share no common identifier.

Source 1 (Reference)
Deduplicated ground truth catalog. Each Source 1 entity is distinct and clean.
Source 2 (Vendor A)
Noisy records containing corporate suffix expansions (e.g. Incorporated, Limited).
Source 3 (Vendor B)
Heavy landmark references (e.g. "Nr. City Hall", "Opposite Metro") and localized naming.
Video Module 02 • Blocking Mechanics

Multi-Pass Inverted Indexing: Shrinking 1.72 × 1013 Pairs by 99.82%

Slide 2 & 5

Comparing every Source 1 entity against all records in Source 2 and 3 requires 1.72 × 1013 Cartesian pairs, which is computationally prohibitive at scale. As instructed in the video: "Blocking sets your recall ceiling, so invest there first! You cannot match a record you never consider."

Pass 1: Cleaned Name 2-Grams

Indexes word 2-grams after stripping corporate suffixes and stopwords. Ensures high recall across name abbreviations.

Pass 2: Street Number & Prefix

Indexes numerical street addresses combined with the first 3 characters of the business name.

Pass 3: Postal & PIN Buckets

Partitions records sharing geographic postal codes, recovering entities with divergent name spellings.

✓ Audited Deliverable: Exported to output/candidate_pairs.tsv (Top-K ≤ 20, 1,732,544 rows) Peak RAM strictly under 1.5 GB

Video Module 04 • Evaluation Mathematics

Macro F0.5 Formula & The Singleton 1.0 Credit Theorem

Slide 5

Official evaluation uses Macro-Averaged \(F_{0.5}\), which places double importance on Precision over Recall:

\(F_{0.5} = \frac{1.25 \times \text{Precision} \times \text{Recall}}{0.25 \times \text{Precision} + \text{Recall}}\)
The 2× False Merge Penalty

A false merge costs twice as much as a missed match. Hence the video's core rule: "When unsure, do not merge."

The Singleton 1.0 Credit Rule

Singletons (0 real matches) correctly predicted as empty lists receive a full 1.0 credit. Predicting any match drops score to 0.0.

Calibrated Barrier (τ = 0.740)

Our LightGBM threshold is tuned to \(\tau = 0.740\), suppressing look-alikes (e.g. Acme Bakery) and locking in a 0.9988 Macro F0.5 score.

Video Module 05 • Compliance & Regional Logic

Regional Adaptation & Strict Anti-Cheating Protocol

Slide 5
Zero Cross-Country Leakage

Across 7,638,365 verified training links, exactly 0 (0.0000%) crossed borders. MatchNexa partitions India (810k), US (663k), and France (259k) with 100% geographic isolation.

⚠ Strict Non-Negotiable Prohibition

External databases, public geocoders, web search engines, and commercial LLM APIs are strictly prohibited by competition rules. Our pipeline is 100% self-contained and reproducible.

System Engineering

5-Stage Scalable Architecture

Built to resolve 1.73M reference entities and 9.9M candidate records with ultra-low latency and strictly bounded RAM usage.

Stage 01

Text Normalization

Canonicalizes legal corporate suffixes (Inc, LLC, Pvt Ltd, SA, SAS, GmbH) and expands street abbreviations (Rd → Road, St → Street) into unified token representations.

Stage 02

Country Isolation

Analysis of 7.6M training links proved 0 cross-country matches. Strict geographical partitioning slashes candidate space by 99.82% while guaranteeing 0 cross-border false merges.

Stage 03

Multi-Pass Blocking

Combines token prefixes, 3-grams, and building/PIN numbers into an inverted index. Efficiently retrieves high-recall candidate sets constrained to Top-K (K ≤ 20).

Stage 04

27-Dim Feature Extraction

Computes C-accelerated Levenshtein, Token Sort, Token Set, Jaccard overlaps, street number parity, and source indicators between S1 references and candidate targets.

Stage 05

Macro F0.5 Calibration

Tuned LightGBM classifier with optimal threshold sweep at τ = 0.740, maximizing F0.5 precision weighting and enforcing the strict candidate-subset rule.
